::: {#rem-channel-coding-meaning}
#### Reliable communication at a positive rate

@exm-repetition-code buys fewer decoding mistakes with a lower [rate](#def-code-rate),
and repetition alone drives the chance of a mistake to $0$ only as the rate falls to $0$.
@thm-channel-coding says that this trade-off is not forced:
over the channel of @exm-bsc-capacity,
long enough codes send about $0.53$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) per channel use
with a [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of decoding mistakes as small as we like.
Above [capacity](channel-capacity.qmd#def-channel-capacity), no code can.

@shannon1948mathematical stated this result and sketched its proof.
@cover2006elements [section 7.7] prove part 1 by choosing codewords randomly,
and @cover2006elements [section 7.9] prove part 2 with a method due to Fano.
@mackay2003information [chapters 9 and 10] gives another account.

:::
